text: Did you know that everything that Diogo says is a topaz?
WARIO WORLD IS GOOD!
The ocean covers about 71% of the Earth's surface, yet over 80% of it remains completely unexplored. Nobody knows what is down there.
The Blue Whale is the largest animal to have ever lived on Earth. Its heart alone is the size of a small car and you could crawl through its arteries.
The Mariana Trench is nearly 36,000 feet deep. If you dropped Mount Everest into it, the peak would still be over a mile underwater.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and nine brains. They are basically aliens that decided to live underwater instead.
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they do not drift away from each other. You will never be loved like that.
The pistol shrimp can snap its claw fast enough to create a bubble hotter than the surface of the Sun. It is a tiny murderer and nothing can stop it.
Sharks are older than trees. They have existed for about 450 million years. Trees only showed up around 350 million years ago. Sharks were here first.
The Atlantic Ocean grows about one inch wider every year. Not useful information. Just thought you should know.
Jellyfish have no brain, no heart, no blood, and no bones. They are 95% water and have survived five mass extinction events. What is their secret.
The ocean produces over 50% of the world's oxygen. So next time you breathe, thank the sea, not a tree.
Clownfish can change gender. The dominant fish in any group is always female. Finding Nemo got the science completely wrong.
A group of jellyfish is officially called a smack. Scientists were clearly having a great day when they named that one.
The blobfish only looks like a sad deflated lump because it gets decompressed when pulled from deep water. In its natural habitat it looks completely normal. Pressure does things to you.
Mantis shrimp have 16 types of colour receptors. Humans have 3. Mantis shrimp are perceiving a version of reality we cannot even comprehend.
There are more historical artefacts on the ocean floor than in all of the world's museums combined. The sea is a hoarder.
Dolphins have unique whistles they use as names to call each other. They also bully other animals for fun. Very relatable creatures.
The coelacanth is a fish scientists thought went extinct 65 million years ago. Then one turned up alive in 1938. The ocean had it the whole time and said nothing.
The sound you hear when you hold a shell to your ear is not the ocean. It is ambient noise resonating in the cavity. You have been lied to your whole life.
Whale songs can travel thousands of miles through the ocean. They are calling out into the void hoping someone hears them. Same, whale.
Starfish do not have blood. They pump seawater through their bodies instead. They can also regrow entire limbs which is deeply unfair.
The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's landmass combined. It is just sitting there being massive and showing off.
There are lakes and rivers under the ocean. Underwater bodies of water sitting inside water. The ocean does whatever it wants.
Sea cucumbers breathe through their rear ends. They can also expel their own internal organs as a defence mechanism. Nature is disgusting and I respect it.
The immortal jellyfish can revert back to its juvenile state after reaching maturity. It is biologically immortal. We are out here dying and jellyfish found the cheat code.
Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support about 25% of all marine species. They are doing a lot of heavy lifting.
The mimic octopus can impersonate over 15 different species including lionfish, flatfish, and sea snakes. It is the greatest actor in the ocean.
Anglerfish that you see in pictures are all female. The males are tiny parasites that fuse to the female's body permanently. Romantic.
There are volcanoes all over the ocean floor. The ocean has entire mountain ranges you will never see and entire eruptions nobody notices.
The dumbo octopus lives deeper than almost any other octopus, up to 13,000 feet down. It flaps ear-like fins to swim. It is adorable and lives in absolute darkness.
Some deep sea fish produce their own light through a process called bioluminescence. They are glowing in the pitch black at the bottom of the world. Respect.
The Amazon Rainforest produces about 20% of the world's oxygen. It is called the lungs of the Earth. We are currently setting it on fire.
A new species is discovered in the Amazon roughly every 3 days. Most of them are insects. Most of them want to kill you.
Poison dart frogs are only poisonous in the wild because of the specific insects they eat. Raised in captivity they are completely harmless. Environment matters.
The rafflesia flower is the world's largest flower and smells exactly like rotting flesh to attract flies for pollination. Nature has no dignity.
Jaguars are the only big cats that kill prey by biting directly through the skull. They do not mess around.
Trees in a rainforest communicate with each other through an underground fungal network. Scientists call it the Wood Wide Web. Trees invented the internet first.

The bullet ant has the most painful sting of any insect on Earth. It feels like a burning nail being driven into your flesh for 24 straight hours. Some tribes make boys wear gloves full of them as a rite of passage.
Sloths are so slow that algae grows on their fur. They essentially have their own ecosystem living on top of them at all times.
There are more species of insects in one square mile of Amazon rainforest than in the entire United Kingdom. Horrifying.
The titan arum plant blooms once every several years and releases a smell like rotting corpses when it does. People line up around the block to see it. Humanity is something else.
The electric eel is not actually an eel. It is more closely related to catfish and carp. Everything you knew was wrong.
Anacondas can go months without eating after a large meal. After swallowing a whole deer they just sit there doing nothing for weeks. Goals.
Capybaras are the world's largest rodents and get along with literally every other animal. Ducks, monkeys, caimans, everyone loves capybaras. Learn from them.
The walking palm tree can slowly move up to 20 metres a year by growing new roots and letting old ones die. It literally walks. Slowly. But still.
Gorillas make a brand new sleeping nest every single night. They never sleep in the same spot twice. The ultimate no-commitment lifestyle.
Leaf-cutter ants have been farming fungus for over 50 million years. Humans invented agriculture about 10,000 years ago. Ants were already running farms before we existed.
The glass frog has a completely transparent belly. You can see its heart beating and its stomach digesting food in real time. Nature said no privacy.
Over 25% of medicines used today were originally discovered in rainforest plants. We keep burning those plants down before we can study them. Cool.
Rubber trees are native to the Amazon. The rubber in your tyres, your shoes, and your other rubber items all started in the jungle.
Some jungle tribes have been living completely isolated from the modern world for thousands of years. They are fine. Leave them alone.
Piranhas are actually mostly scavengers. The bloodthirsty killer fish reputation is largely a myth started by Theodore Roosevelt after a staged feeding. Thanks Teddy.
The harpy eagle is the largest eagle in the Americas. Its talons are bigger than a grizzly bear's claws and it hunts monkeys. It does not mess around.
Chocolate comes from the cacao tree which only grows in tropical regions. Cocoa beans were used as currency by the Aztecs. Money you can eat was the correct system.
Ants outnumber humans by roughly 20 quadrillion to 8 billion. They have already won. We just have not figured it out yet.
The Amazon river discharges so much fresh water into the Atlantic Ocean that you can drink the water 100 miles out to sea. The river was not done.
Vampire bats are real and live in South American jungles. They drink blood yes. But they also adopt orphaned bats and share food with hungry roostmates. Wholesome vampires.
The blue morpho butterfly has wings that appear bright blue but contain no blue pigment. The colour comes entirely from microscopic structures reflecting light. It is an illusion.
Some fig trees can only be pollinated by one specific species of wasp. If that wasp goes extinct, the tree goes extinct. They are completely dependent on each other. Terrifying.
The hoatzin bird smells like cow manure because of how it digests food. It also cannot fly well and has claws on its wings as a baby. It is a mess and it is doing its best.
Army ants have no permanent home. They are constantly on the move as a massive living colony that eats everything in their path and builds temporary structures out of their own bodies.
The first computer bug was an actual bug. A moth was found stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II in 1947. Grace Hopper taped it into the log book and called it a bug. The term stuck.
The first domain name ever registered was Symbolics.com on March 15th 1985. It is still active. It is a museum now.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was originally designed to slow typists down to prevent typewriter jams. Typewriters no longer exist. We kept the slow keyboard anyway. Nobody questioned it.
The average smartphone today has more computing power than all of NASA had when they sent humans to the moon. You are using yours to watch videos of people falling over.
There are approximately 1.13 billion websites on the internet. About 82% of them are inactive. The internet is mostly a graveyard.
The word robot comes from a 1920 Czech play. It means forced labour. The people who named them knew exactly what they were doing.
The first computer password was invented at MIT in the 1960s. Someone immediately printed the entire password file and handed it out to people. Security was not a priority back then.
Email is older than the World Wide Web. Ray Tomlinson sent the first email in 1971. He cannot remember what it said. It was probably spam.
The Firefox browser logo is not actually a fox. It is a red panda. The name Firefox comes from the red panda's Chinese nickname. You have been looking at a red panda this whole time.
The first webcam was pointed at a coffee pot at Cambridge University so researchers could check if there was coffee without walking to the kitchen. Technology at its finest.
Samsung was founded in 1938 as a grocery store selling noodles and dried fish. Now they make your phone. Interesting pivot.
Nintendo was founded in 1889 making playing cards. Before video games they tried running a taxi company, a love hotel, and selling instant rice. None of it worked so they made Mario instead.
The inventor of the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee, gave it to the entire world for free and refused to patent it. He has since said he regrets some things about how it turned out. Fair enough.
The first hard drive ever made in 1956 was the size of two refrigerators and held 5 megabytes of data. Your phone holds about a million times more and fits in your pocket.
There are more transistors on a modern CPU than there are stars in the Milky Way galaxy. Chip manufacturers casually build things more complex than galaxies.
The term debugging in computing literally comes from Grace Hopper removing that moth from the relay in 1947. One bug changed the vocabulary of an entire industry.

Wikipedia is maintained almost entirely by volunteers. There are more articles than any one person could read in a lifetime. Most of the editing is done by a surprisingly small group of obsessive people.
The original iPhone in 2007 did not support third-party apps. Steve Jobs said the web browser was enough. He was wrong and changed his mind a year later.
Google was almost named BackRub. They ran a search engine called BackRub for two years before changing the name. The world narrowly avoided saying BackRub it.
The first video game ever sold commercially was Computer Space in 1971. It flopped because it was too complicated. Pong came out a year later and was a massive hit. Keep it simple.
About 90% of all data in the world was created in the last two years. We are generating information faster than any civilisation in history and most of it is garbage.
The entire text of Wikipedia in English takes up about 21 gigabytes. A modern graphics card has more memory than that just to render one frame of a video game.

Bluetooth is named after a 10th century Danish king called Harald Bluetooth who was famous for uniting tribes. The technology unites devices. Someone at the naming meeting was very pleased with themselves.
The programming language Python is named after Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake. Guido van Rossum was reading Monty Python scripts when he created it.
There are more lines of code in a modern car than in a passenger jet. Your car is more software than machine at this point.
The first commercial text message was sent on December 3rd 1992. It said Merry Christmas. The person who sent it could not reply because phones could not send texts yet, only receive them.
AutoCorrect was invented in the early 1990s inside Microsoft Word. It was originally just to fix common typos like teh and adn. It has since become a source of endless suffering.
The USB logo has a trident design based on Neptune's trident, chosen to represent the power of the technology. Every time you flip a USB upside down three times before it fits, remember that.
The average person unlocks their phone about 80 to 150 times per day. Nobody decided this was a good use of human attention. It just happened.
CD-ROMs were originally designed to hold exactly 74 minutes of audio because that was the length of Beethoven's 9th Symphony. A Sony executive insisted on it. Classical music shaped data storage.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus. It rotates so slowly that it completes an orbit around the Sun before it finishes one full rotation. Venus does not care about your calendar.
There are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches combined. And the observable universe is only a fraction of the whole thing.

If the Sun were the size of a front door, the Earth would be the size of a coin. If the Sun were the size of a front door, the largest known star would be taller than Mount Everest. We are very small.
Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about 10 million tons. They are the collapsed cores of dead stars and they are terrifying.
The footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the Moon will remain there for at least 10 million years because there is no wind or weather to disturb them.
Space is completely silent. Sound needs a medium to travel through and space is a vacuum. Every explosion, collision, and death in space happens in total silence.
There is a planet called 55 Cancri e where it may literally rain rocks. The surface temperature is around 2700 degrees Celsius. Scientists named it a super-Earth. Optimistic naming.
The International Space Station travels at 17,500 miles per hour. Astronauts on board see 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every single day.
One million Earths could fit inside the Sun. The Sun itself is considered an average-sized star. Some stars are so large a billion Suns could fit inside them.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft launched in 1977 and is still operating. It is currently over 23 billion kilometres from Earth and is the most distant man-made object ever built.

Black holes do not actually suck things in. They simply have gravity like any other object. If the Sun suddenly became a black hole, Earth would continue orbiting in the same path. We would just freeze.
There is a gas cloud in the constellation Sagittarius that contains billions of litres of alcohol. It also smells like raspberries. The universe is full of surprises.
Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system. Olympus Mons is about the size of France and three times the height of Mount Everest. Mars went very hard on volcanoes.
The Sun accounts for 99.86% of all the mass in the solar system. Everything else, all the planets, moons, asteroids, and comets, makes up the remaining 0.14%.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. When you look at the Sun you are seeing it as it was 8 minutes ago. When you look at distant stars you are looking back thousands of years.
Pluto was considered a planet for 76 years before being reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. Many people took this personally. Pluto does not care. It is still out there.
There are more possible iterations of a game of chess than there are atoms in the observable universe. The universe is large but chess players are exhausting.
Saturn's rings are not solid. They are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock ranging from tiny grains to chunks the size of houses. From a distance it looks like a solid disk.
The coldest place ever recorded in the universe is the Boomerang Nebula at minus 272 degrees Celsius. That is colder than the natural background temperature of deep space itself.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm that has been raging for at least 350 years. It is currently shrinking but at its largest it was three times the size of Earth.
On Mercury a single day lasts longer than its entire year. It rotates very slowly but orbits the Sun quite quickly. Time on Mercury is a complete disaster.
The Moon is moving away from Earth at about 3.8 centimetres per year. In the distant past the Moon was much closer and days on Earth were only about 6 hours long.
There is a planet called WASP-12b that is being slowly eaten by its own star. It orbits so close that the star's gravity is pulling the planet apart. It has about 3 million years left.
Water exists all over the solar system. It has been found on the Moon, Mars, Europa, and in comets. Water is not rare. Life might not be either.
The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. Earth is 4.5 billion years old. Humans have existed for about 300,000 years. We showed up very late.
Astronauts grow up to 2 inches taller in space because the spine decompresses without gravity. They shrink back down when they return to Earth.
The Milky Way galaxy is on a collision course with the Andromeda galaxy. They will merge in about 4.5 billion years. The Sun and Earth will likely survive. Nobody you know will be around to see it.
There is so much empty space inside an atom that if you removed it all, every atom in every human being on Earth would compress into a cube smaller than a sugar cube.
NASA's Hubble Space Telescope once pointed at a completely dark patch of sky for 10 days. The image revealed over 3,000 previously unknown galaxies in that single tiny spot of nothing.

Time passes slightly faster for the GPS satellites orbiting Earth than it does for us on the surface. Without Einstein's theory of relativity correcting for this, GPS would drift by about 10 kilometres every day.
The word mafia is never spoken once in The Godfather. Francis Ford Coppola made a deal with the Italian-American Civil Rights League to avoid using it.
The shower scene in Psycho used chocolate syrup for blood because it showed up better on black and white film. Janet Leigh did not actually shower for months after filming it.
The lion roar used in the MGM logo is not actually a lion roaring. It is a recording of a tiger. The most famous lion in Hollywood history is a tiger.

James Cameron spent more of his own money building the Titanic set than the actual Titanic cost to build when adjusted for inflation. The film cost 200 million dollars. The ship cost about 7.5 million in 1912.
The noise lightsabers make in Star Wars was created by combining the hum of an old television set with the buzz of a film projector motor. Ben Burtt discovered it completely by accident.
The T-Rex roar in Jurassic Park is a combination of a baby elephant, a tiger, and an alligator. No actual Tyrannosaurus was available for recording unfortunately.

The cast of Goodfellas was told to improvise a lot of their dialogue. The famous is he funny to you scene was completely unscripted. Joe Pesci based it on a real story from when he worked at a restaurant.
Heath Ledger locked himself in a hotel room for a month to prepare for the Joker role in The Dark Knight. He kept a diary in character and barely slept. The performance won him a posthumous Oscar.
The alien language in Avatar took Paul Frommer three years to create. It has a consistent grammar and over 1000 words. Actors spent months learning to speak it fluently.
The famous chest-bursting scene in Alien was kept secret from most of the cast until it was filmed. Their horrified reactions are completely real. They had no idea what was about to happen.

Stanley Kubrick shot so many takes of Shelley Duvall in The Shining that the Guinness World Record for most takes of a single scene is held by that film. Duvall's hair started falling out from stress.
The budget for Jaws was 3.5 million dollars. It ended up costing 9 million because the mechanical shark kept breaking down. Spielberg had to shoot around it which accidentally made it scarier.
Tom Hanks lost 50 pounds to film the second half of Cast Away. Production paused for a year while he lost the weight. He also learned to crack open coconuts and start fires for real.
The horse head in The Godfather was real. Coppola obtained an actual horse head from a dog food company. Nobody told Marlon Brando it would be real and his reaction is genuine.
The budget for Mad Max: Fury Road was 185 million dollars and took 17 years to make. About 80% of what you see on screen is practical effects and real stunts. Almost no green screen.

The entire script for Parasite was written by Bong Joon-ho over the course of four years. He storyboarded every single shot before filming began. The film won four Academy Awards including Best Picture.
The rotating hallway fight scene in Inception was built as a real physical set that could actually rotate 360 degrees. The actors and stunt crew trained for weeks to film in it.
Daniel Day-Lewis stayed in character as Abraham Lincoln for the entire duration of filming Lincoln. He refused to break character between takes and communicated with crew members by written note.
The flying sequences in E.T. were filmed by pointing the camera up at the actors in front of a lit sky backdrop. The moon silhouette shot was a painting on glass placed in front of the lens.

The Wilhelm Scream is a stock sound effect recorded in 1951 that has been used in hundreds of films and TV shows. Once you know what it sounds like you will hear it everywhere and never stop noticing it.

Cary Grant's distinctive speaking accent is not British or American. He invented it himself as a young actor because he thought his real Bristol accent sounded wrong. The accent became so famous it influenced how people spoke.
The film Cleopatra in 1963 was so expensive it nearly bankrupted 20th Century Fox. It cost 44 million dollars which in today's money would be over 400 million. It made all of that back and then some.
The Matrix was rejected by every major studio before Warner Bros picked it up. The Wachowskis had to make a short film to prove they could direct action. The short film was the opening scene.
Every Disney animated film from The Little Mermaid onwards contains a hidden Mickey Mouse symbol somewhere in it. Finding them all is a thing people genuinely spend time doing.
Psycho was the first American film to show a toilet flushing on screen. The censors were furious about it. This was apparently the controversial moment of 1960.

The actor who played Darth Vader's body, David Prowse, was not told that James Earl Jones would voice the character. He recorded all his dialogue on set and only found out his voice was replaced at the premiere.

The entire production of Apocalypse Now was a disaster. Martin Sheen had a heart attack. The sets were destroyed by a typhoon. Marlon Brando showed up overweight and having read nothing. The film still won two Oscars.
The running scene in Forrest Gump where he runs across America took four months to film. Tom Hanks actually ran every single step shown on screen. No stunt doubles were used for the running.
The word of the day in the film industry is cut because early films were literally cut with scissors to edit them together. The physical act of cutting film gave us all modern editing terminology.
Roger Deakins has been nominated for the Academy Award for Best Cinematography 16 times. He won on his 14th nomination for Blade Runner 2049. The Academy made him wait a very long time.
